canonical_goal.outcome_variable: o_dir = (D,S_0,E_dir) ∈ O_P^{dir}, where D is a lattice dimension, S_0 is a finite set of canonical SU(2) Wilson-loop classes, and E_dir is a finite linearly independent set of Q(λ)-linear equations in the variables {w(C): C∈S_0}
canonical_goal.target_object: A complete linearly independent basis E_dir for the direct algebraic row space R_dir(D,S_0) over Q(λ), where R_dir(D,S_0) consists exactly of equations among normalized SU(2) Wilson-loop expectation values w(C)=(1/2)⟨tr(∏_{e∈C}U_e)⟩ whose variables all belong to a finite canonical target set S_0 after canonicalization. The row space R_dir(D,S_0) is the Q(λ)-span of two retained row families: (1) every row obtained from the link-variation identity ∫DU δ_ε(μ)[exp(-S)W_x^{ab}(μ,C)] = 0, equivalently -⟨W_x^{ab}(μ,C)δ_εS⟩+⟨δ_εW_x^{ab}(μ,C)⟩=0, with SU(2) Wilson action S=-(1/λ)Σ_P tr(U_P+U_P^†), after rewriting each produced single-trace term as w(canon(C′)) and retaining the row only when canon(C′)∈S_0 for every produced C′; and (2) every row obtained by applying the SU(2) trace identity tr(X)tr(Y)=tr(XY)+tr(XY^†) to based subloops X,Y and equating two canonicalized single-trace sums whenever they correspond to the same canonical double-trace operator and every resulting single-trace variable lies in S_0.
feasibility_constraints: D∈{2,3,4}; the lattice is the D-dimensional hypercubic Euclidean lattice with directed edge alphabet A_D={±e_1,…,±e_D}; a closed loop word C=(c_1,…,c_L) has c_i∈A_D and total displacement Σ_{i=1}^L c_i=0.

The gauge group is SU(2), so each link variable U_μ(x) is a 2×2 special unitary matrix, the plaquette variable is U_P=U_μ(x)U_ν(x+μ_hat)U_μ(x+ν_hat)^†U_ν(x)^†, and the Wilson action is S=-(1/λ)Σ_P tr(U_P+U_P^†), which is the paper's S=-(N/(2λ))Σ_P tr(U_P+U_P^†) after substituting N=2.
For every closed loop word C, W(C)=tr(∏_{i=1}^L U_{c_i}) and w(C)=(1/2)⟨W(C)⟩ with w(empty loop)=1; length(C)=L is the number of directed letters in C.

The map canon(C) returns the unique representative of the equivalence class of C under cyclic rotation of the word, reversal with inversion of every directed edge, and hypercubic rotations/reflections of the lattice axes; a canonical representative contains no adjacent inverse pair c_{i+1}=-c_i, including the cyclic adjacency c_1=-c_L.
S_0 is any finite subset of canonical loop classes, and every equation row in E_dir is a finite Q(λ)-linear combination Σ_{C∈S_0} a_C(λ)w(C)+a_∅(λ)=0 with a_C(λ),a_∅(λ)∈Q(λ).

A link-variation row is feasible only if it is produced from ∫DU δ_ε(μ)[exp(-S)W_x^{ab}(μ,C)]=0, all double-trace terms have been reduced using tr(X)tr(Y)=tr(XY)+tr(XY^†), and every resulting single-trace loop word C′ satisfies canon(C′)∈S_0.

A trace row is feasible only if two decompositions of possibly self-intersecting based loop words into based subloops X,Y yield the same canonical double-trace operator, the SU(2) identity tr(X)tr(Y)=tr(XY)+tr(XY^†) converts each decomposition into a sum of canonical single-trace variables, and every such variable lies in S_0.

success_set.definition: Σ_dir = { o_dir=(D,S_0,E_dir) : D∈{2,3,4}; S_0 is a finite set of canonical closed loop words on the D-dimensional hypercubic lattice; E_dir is linearly independent over Q(λ); and span_Q(λ)(E_dir)=R_dir(D,S_0), where R_dir(D,S_0) is the Q(λ)-span of exactly the following retained rows. Family A contains every row generated by ∫DU δ_ε(μ)[exp(-S)W_x^{ab}(μ,C)]=0, equivalently -⟨W_x^{ab}(μ,C)δ_εS⟩+⟨δ_εW_x^{ab}(μ,C)⟩=0, with S=-(1/λ)Σ_P tr(U_P+U_P^†), after reducing SU(2) double traces via tr(X)tr(Y)=tr(XY)+tr(XY^†), mapping each produced loop word C′ to canon(C′), and requiring canon(C′)∈S_0 for every produced single-trace term. Family B contains every row generated by two based subloop decompositions that give the same canonical double-trace operator, after using tr(X)tr(Y)=tr(XY)+tr(XY^†) to express each decomposition as a sum of canonical single-trace variables, and requiring every such variable to lie in S_0. }

robustness_scope.ambient_space: All finite pairs (D,S_0) with D∈{2,3,4} and S_0 a finite set of canonical SU(2) Wilson-loop classes on the D-dimensional hypercubic lattice; each coordinate variable is w(C)=(1/2)⟨tr(∏_{e∈C}U_e)⟩.
robustness_scope.indexing_set: I_dir = { (D,S_0) : D∈{2,3,4} and S_0 is a finite subset of canonical closed SU(2) Wilson-loop classes on the D-dimensional hypercubic lattice }

claimed_subfamily.definition: For every (D,S_0)∈I_dir, the claimed subfamily consists of the direct row space R_dir(D,S_0) generated by retained link-variation rows from ∫DU δ_ε(μ)[exp(-S)W_x^{ab}(μ,C)]=0 with S=-(1/λ)Σ_P tr(U_P+U_P^†), retained trace rows from tr(X)tr(Y)=tr(XY)+tr(XY^†), canonicalization under cyclic rotation, reversal, and hypercubic rotations/reflections, and the retention condition that every produced single-trace representative lies in S_0.

hinted_superfamily.definition: A larger not-proved family replaces SU(2) by another compact gauge group and replaces tr(X)tr(Y)=tr(XY)+tr(XY^†) by the corresponding finite polynomial trace identities for that group while keeping finite canonical Wilson-loop target sets on hypercubic lattices.

robustness_scope.criterion: For every indexed pair (D,S_0), success is the span equality span_Q(λ)(E_dir)=R_dir(D,S_0), where R_dir(D,S_0) is generated only by retained rows from ∫DU δ_ε(μ)[exp(-S)W_x^{ab}(μ,C)]=0 with S=-(1/λ)Σ_P tr(U_P+U_P^†) and retained rows from tr(X)tr(Y)=tr(XY)+tr(XY^†), after canonicalizing all produced loop words and discarding any row with a produced single-trace representative outside S_0.

canonical_goal.outcome_variable: o_ind = (D,S_0,S_1,E_proj,E_ind) ∈ O_P^{ind}, where S_0⊂S_1 are finite canonical SU(2) Wilson-loop sets, E_proj is a finite projected row-space basis on S_0, and E_ind is a quotient-basis of projected rows not already generated directly inside S_0
canonical_goal.target_object: A linearly independent representative basis E_ind for the indirect quotient row space I(D,S_0,S_1)=P(D,S_0,S_1)/R_dir(D,S_0), where S_0⊂S_1 are finite canonical SU(2) loop sets. R_dir(D,S) denotes the Q(λ)-row space generated in a finite set S by retained rows from ∫DU δ_ε(μ)[exp(-S_YM)W_x^{ab}(μ,C)]=0 with S_YM=-(1/λ)Σ_P tr(U_P+U_P^†), together with retained rows from tr(X)tr(Y)=tr(XY)+tr(XY^†), after canonicalizing all produced loop words and requiring every produced single-trace representative to lie in S. P(D,S_0,S_1) is the projected row space on variables x={w(C):C∈S_0} induced by eliminating auxiliary variables y={w(C):C∈S_1\S_0} from R_dir(D,S_1). Formally, if a matrix whose rows span R_dir(D,S_1) is partitioned as A_x x + A_y y = 0 over Q(λ), then P(D,S_0,S_1)={ r^T A_x x = 0 : r is a row-combination vector over Q(λ) and r^T A_y=0 }; E_ind is a basis of this projected space modulo the rows already in R_dir(D,S_0). This target is the resulting finite algebraic constraint space, not the search heuristic used to find it.
feasibility_constraints: D∈{2,3,4}; S_0 and S_1 are finite subsets of canonical SU(2) Wilson-loop classes on the D-dimensional hypercubic lattice; S_0⊂S_1; every coordinate variable has the form w(C)=(1/2)⟨tr(∏_{e∈C}U_e)⟩.

The direct row space R_dir(D,S_1) is generated only by retained rows from ∫DU δ_ε(μ)[exp(-S)W_x^{ab}(μ,C)]=0 with S=-(1/λ)Σ_P tr(U_P+U_P^†) and retained rows from tr(X)tr(Y)=tr(XY)+tr(XY^†), after canonicalizing all produced loop words and requiring every produced single-trace representative to lie in S_1.
Let x enumerate {w(C):C∈S_0} and y enumerate {w(C):C∈S_1\S_0}; every row in R_dir(D,S_1) can be written as one row of A_x x + A_y y = 0 with entries in Q(λ).

The projected row space P(D,S_0,S_1) contains exactly those Q(λ)-linear equations in x obtained from row-combination vectors r satisfying r^T A_y=0; this condition eliminates every auxiliary variable in y and leaves only variables indexed by S_0.

E_proj is feasible only if span_Q(λ)(E_proj)=P(D,S_0,S_1) and E_proj is row-independent over Q(λ); E_ind is feasible only if its image is a row-independent basis of the quotient P(D,S_0,S_1)/R_dir(D,S_0).

A finite enlargement S_1 may be described as empirically saturated for S_0 only when a further finite enlargement reported in the same computation does not increase dim_Q(λ)P(D,S_0,S_1); this is a finite-rank observation and not a theorem over all possible supersets.

success_set.definition: Σ_ind = { o_ind=(D,S_0,S_1,E_proj,E_ind) : D∈{2,3,4}; S_0⊂S_1 are finite canonical SU(2) Wilson-loop sets; R_dir(D,S) is, for S=S_0 or S=S_1, the Q(λ)-row space generated by retained rows from ∫DU δ_ε(μ)[exp(-S_YM)W_x^{ab}(μ,C)]=0 with S_YM=-(1/λ)Σ_P tr(U_P+U_P^†) and retained rows from tr(X)tr(Y)=tr(XY)+tr(XY^†), after canonicalizing produced loop words and requiring produced single-trace representatives to lie in S; after writing a row-spanning matrix for R_dir(D,S_1) as A_x x + A_y y=0 with x={w(C):C∈S_0} and y={w(C):C∈S_1\S_0}, span_Q(λ)(E_proj)={r^T A_x x=0 : r^T A_y=0}; E_proj is linearly independent; and E_ind is a linearly independent representative basis of {r^T A_x x=0 : r^T A_y=0}/R_dir(D,S_0). }

robustness_scope.ambient_space: Finite triples (D,S_0,S_1) with D∈{2,3,4}, S_0 a finite canonical SU(2) Wilson-loop target set, and S_1 a finite canonical auxiliary superset containing S_0; variables in S_1\S_0 are eliminable auxiliary coordinates.
robustness_scope.indexing_set: I_ind = { (D,S_0,S_1) : D∈{2,3,4}, S_0⊂S_1, and S_0,S_1 are finite canonical SU(2) Wilson-loop sets on the D-dimensional hypercubic lattice }

claimed_subfamily.definition: The claimed subfamily consists of finite SU(2) cases computed by forming, in an enlarged finite canonical loop set S_1, a row space generated by retained rows from ∫DU δ_ε(μ)[exp(-S_YM)W_x^{ab}(μ,C)]=0 with S_YM=-(1/λ)Σ_P tr(U_P+U_P^†) and retained rows from tr(X)tr(Y)=tr(XY)+tr(XY^†), partitioning a row-spanning matrix as A_x x + A_y y=0 with x indexed by S_0 and y indexed by S_1\S_0, and projecting to S_0 by row-combination vectors r satisfying r^T A_y=0; completeness is claimed only relative to the finite auxiliary sets actually used and is described as empirical saturation when further reported finite enlargements add no projected rank.

robustness_scope.criterion: For each indexed triple (D,S_0,S_1), define R_dir(D,S_0) as the Q(λ)-row space generated inside S_0 by retained rows from ∫DU δ_ε(μ)[exp(-S_YM)W_x^{ab}(μ,C)]=0 with S_YM=-(1/λ)Σ_P tr(U_P+U_P^†) and retained rows from tr(X)tr(Y)=tr(XY)+tr(XY^†). Define P(D,S_0,S_1)={r^T A_x x=0 : r^T A_y=0}, where A_x x + A_y y=0 is a row-spanning matrix for the same retained-row construction inside S_1, x indexes S_0, and y indexes S_1\S_0. Success requires span_Q(λ)(E_proj)=P(D,S_0,S_1), requires E_ind to be exactly a basis of P(D,S_0,S_1)/R_dir(D,S_0), forbids variables w(C) with C∈S_1\S_0 in any row of E_ind, and forbids rows already in R_dir(D,S_0) from counting as indirect quotient rows.

canonical_goal.outcome_variable: o_count = (D,L,ℓ,M_exact,N_loop,N_SD,N_Tr,N_All,N_proj,R,F_loop,F_eqn) ∈ O_P^{count}, where ℓ is an exact even loop length, L is an even cumulative cutoff length, and the remaining components are integer counts, ranks, ratios, or proposed asymptotic forms
canonical_goal.target_object: A finite enumeration and large-L growth characterization for SU(2) canonical Wilson-loop variables and independent loop-equation ranks on D-dimensional hypercubic lattices with D∈{2,3,4}. The enumeration separates exact-length shape counts M_exact(D,ℓ), where ℓ is a fixed even loop length and lower-dimensional embeddable classes are excluded when reporting genuinely 3D or genuinely 4D strata, from cumulative cutoff counts N_loop(D,L)=|S[L]|, where S[L] contains all canonical loop classes of length at most an even cutoff L in the chosen D-dimensional lattice. The equation ranks are N_SD(D,L), N_Tr(D,L), and N_All(D,L), defined as Q(λ)-ranks inside S[L] of rows from ∫DU δ_ε(μ)[exp(-S_YM)W_x^{ab}(μ,C)]=0 with S_YM=-(1/λ)Σ_P tr(U_P+U_P^†), rows from tr(X)tr(Y)=tr(XY)+tr(XY^†), and the union of those two row families, respectively; N_proj(D,L,k) is the Q(λ)-rank of projected rows {r^T A_x x=0:r^T A_y=0} from S[L+k] onto S[L]. The growth characterization records the proposed loop-count form F_loop(D,L)=A_D L^{-(1+D/2)}(2D-1)^L and the proposed two-dimensional direct-equation form F_eqn(2,L)=A_2 L^{-2}3^L(1-c/L^δ).
feasibility_constraints: D∈{2,3,4}; ℓ and L are positive even integers; a canonical loop class is a closed edge word modulo cyclic rotation, reversal with edge inversion, and hypercubic rotations/reflections, with immediate adjacent inverse pairs removed.

M_exact(D,ℓ) counts canonical loop classes of exactly ℓ directed edges; when dimension strata are reported, the 3D stratum excludes classes embeddable in any 2D coordinate subspace, and the 4D stratum excludes classes embeddable in any 2D or 3D coordinate subspace.

S[L] is the finite cumulative set of canonical SU(2) Wilson-loop classes whose canonical word length is at most L; N_loop(D,L)=|S[L]| counts the variables w(C)=(1/2)⟨tr(∏_{e∈C}U_e)⟩ indexed by C∈S[L].

N_SD(D,L) is the Q(λ)-rank of retained link-variation rows inside S[L] generated from ∫DU δ_ε(μ)[exp(-S)W_x^{ab}(μ,C)]=0 with S=-(1/λ)Σ_P tr(U_P+U_P^†); N_Tr(D,L) is the Q(λ)-rank of retained trace rows inside S[L] generated from tr(X)tr(Y)=tr(XY)+tr(XY^†); N_All(D,L) is the Q(λ)-rank of the union of these two row sets.
For even k>0, N_proj(D,L,k) is the Q(λ)-rank of {r^T A_x x=0 : r^T A_y=0}, where A_x x + A_y y=0 is the direct-equation matrix inside S[L+k], x indexes S[L], and y indexes S[L+k]\S[L].

The ratio R(D,L)=N_All(D,L)/N_loop(D,L) is defined only when N_loop(D,L)>0; the proposed loop-growth ansatz F_loop(D,L)=A_D L^{-(1+D/2)}(2D-1)^L uses the non-backtracking branching factor 2D-1, a displayed closure factor L^{-D/2}, and a displayed cyclic-quotient factor L^{-1}; the proposed two-dimensional equation-growth ansatz F_eqn(2,L)=A_2 L^{-2}3^L(1-c/L^δ) uses R(2,L)≤1 as the asymptotic bounded-ratio constraint.

success_set.definition: Σ_count = { o_count : for every reported exact-length pair (D,ℓ), M_exact(D,ℓ) equals the number of canonical closed loop-word classes of exact length ℓ after quotienting by cyclic rotation, reversal with edge inversion, and hypercubic rotations/reflections, with the stated exclusion of lower-dimensional embeddable classes for the genuinely 3D and genuinely 4D strata; for every reported cutoff pair (D,L), N_loop(D,L)=|S[L]| where S[L] is the cumulative set of canonical classes of length at most L; N_SD(D,L), N_Tr(D,L), and N_All(D,L) equal the Q(λ)-ranks of the retained link-variation row matrix, the retained SU(2) trace row matrix, and their union inside S[L]; N_proj(D,L,k) equals rank_Q(λ){r^T A_x x=0:r^T A_y=0} for the direct-equation matrix in S[L+k] when projected counts are reported; R(D,L)=N_All(D,L)/N_loop(D,L); F_loop(D,L)=A_D L^{-(1+D/2)}(2D-1)^L is the proposed large-L loop-count form; and F_eqn(2,L)=A_2 L^{-2}3^L(1-c/L^δ) is the proposed large-L two-dimensional direct-equation-count form. }

robustness_scope.indexing_set: I_count = { (D,ℓ,L,k) : D∈{2,3,4}, ℓ and L are positive even integers appearing in the reported finite enumerations, and k is a positive even auxiliary increment appearing in a reported projection table }

methodological_claim.target_object: The paper additionally claims constructive finite procedures for obtaining the end-state row spaces: direct link-variation rows are found by detecting oriented plaquette subwords in canonical loop words, cutting the plaquette, inserting permitted immediately canceling backtrack pairs, varying the marked link, evaluating ∫DU δ_ε(μ)[exp(-S)W_x^{ab}(μ,C)]=0 with S=-(1/λ)Σ_P tr(U_P+U_P^†), reducing SU(2) double traces by tr(X)tr(Y)=tr(XY)+tr(XY^†), and retaining only rows whose produced canonical single-trace variables lie in the target set; direct trace rows are found by cutting self-intersection subloops into double-trace operators and equating the associated canonical single-trace sums when the double-trace labels coincide; projected indirect rows are found by forming a finite auxiliary superset S_1, assembling the direct-equation matrix A_x x + A_y y=0, and computing row combinations r with r^T A_y=0, with a vertex-support filter that keeps an auxiliary loop only when its visited lattice-vertex set is congruent under hypercubic rotations/reflections to the visited lattice-vertex set of at least one target loop.

evidence_channels.formalisation: Let canon(C) identify closed loop words under cyclic rotation, reversal with edge inversion, and hypercubic rotations/reflections. The direct-link procedure enumerates canonical target loops C∈S_0 containing an oriented plaquette subword (μ,ν,-μ,-ν), enumerates inverse cuts that could have produced that plaquette by varying a link or an inserted immediately canceling backtrack pair, evaluates the row from ∫DU δ_ε(μ)[exp(-S)W_x^{ab}(μ,C)]=0 with S=-(1/λ)Σ_P tr(U_P+U_P^†), canonicalizes every produced loop word C′ to canon(C′), and retains the row exactly when every canon(C′) lies in S_0. The direct-trace procedure enumerates based self-intersection decompositions C=AB, assigns the canonical double-trace label {A,B}, forms w(canon(AB))+w(canon(AB^{-1})) using tr(A)tr(B)=tr(AB)+tr(AB^†), and equates two such sums when their canonical double-trace labels coincide. The projected-indirect procedure writes the direct rows in a finite superset S_1 as A_x x + A_y y=0 and outputs all rows r^T A_x x=0 satisfying r^T A_y=0; the vertex-support filter restricts candidate auxiliary loop words C to those for which {vertices visited by C} equals, after a hypercubic rotation/reflection, {vertices visited by C_0} for some C_0∈S_0.

stated_goal.formalisation: The stated goal is to determine, for a finite truncated set S_0 of canonical SU(2) Wilson-loop variables w(C), the algebraic constraint space R_dir(D,S_0)+I(D,S_0,S_1), where R_dir(D,S_0) is generated by retained link-variation rows from ∫DU δ_ε(μ)[exp(-S)W_x^{ab}(μ,C)]=0 and retained SU(2) trace rows from tr(X)tr(Y)=tr(XY)+tr(XY^†), and I(D,S_0,S_1)=P(D,S_0,S_1)/R_dir(D,S_0) with P(D,S_0,S_1)={r^T A_x x=0:r^T A_y=0} after partitioning direct rows in a finite auxiliary superset S_1 as A_x x + A_y y=0. The corresponding independent loop basis is the quotient of span_Q(λ){w(C):C∈S_0} by those direct and projected row constraints.

operational_goal.formalisation: The operational goal is to construct finite Q(λ)-row spaces for canonical SU(2) Wilson-loop variables by: computing R_dir(D,S_0) from retained link-variation and trace rows; computing P(D,S_0,S_1) from row combinations r satisfying r^T A_y=0 in enlarged finite systems A_x x + A_y y=0; reporting exact-length canonical shape counts M_exact(D,ℓ), cumulative target sizes N_loop(D,L)=|S[L]|, direct row ranks N_SD(D,L), N_Tr(D,L), N_All(D,L), projected ranks N_proj(D,L,k), ratios R(D,L), and the proposed growth forms A_D L^{-(1+D/2)}(2D-1)^L and A_2 L^{-2}3^L(1-c/L^δ).

inference_basis: The abstract names the central challenge as determining a dynamically independent basis in a truncated Wilson-loop space and lists direct equations, indirect equations, and counts/growth as the paper's responses.
The introduction frames the problem as an open finite truncation with operator leakage and states that direct and indirect loop-equation categories will be constructed.
Section 3 gives a completeness argument for the direct link-variation rows and a constructive rule for direct SU(2) trace rows within S_0.
Section 5 defines indirect rows as effective relations on S_0 obtained only after eliminating higher-length or auxiliary loops from enlarged direct-equation systems.
Sections 4 and 5 use tables of loop counts, equation ranks, projected ranks, ratios, and fitted growth forms as the quantitative evidence that the constructed row spaces reduce the Wilson-loop basis.
implicit_goal.formalisation: The implicit best-fit goal is the joint conjunction of G1, G2, and G3: construct R_dir(D,S_0), construct I(D,S_0,S_1)=P(D,S_0,S_1)/R_dir(D,S_0), and enumerate or fit the resulting canonical-loop and equation-rank counts. The predictive-fit value is computed from Fit=0.20·TextAlign+0.30·MethodAlign+0.30·EvalAlign+0.20·ClaimAlign−0.05·Complexity using TextAlign=0.96 because nearly all harvested aim spans match this joint goal but some motivation-only spans about first-principles bootstrap and Monte Carlo are excluded, MethodAlign=1.00 because all formal construction components map to direct rows, trace rows, projection, counting, or filtering, EvalAlign=1.00 because all tables and figures report loop counts, row ranks, projected ranks, ratios, or bootstrap-bound effects induced by those rows, ClaimAlign=0.96 because nearly all conclusions concern the same row spaces while future-work claims about systematic seed-rule classification are excluded, and Complexity=0.22 because the populated structural commitments are three robustness scopes plus two additional canonical-goal blocks divided by twenty-three optional structural slots under the rubric's structural-commitment convention. Thus Fit=0.20·0.96+0.30·1.00+0.30·1.00+0.20·0.96−0.05·0.22=0.973.

paper_goal.consistency_relation_derivation: The stated channel's formal aim is a dynamically independent Wilson-loop basis in finite truncations; the operational channel constructs exactly the direct row space R_dir(D,S_0), the projected quotient I(D,S_0,S_1), and the finite counts/ranks that measure basis reduction. Motivational bootstrap framing, Monte Carlo comparison, self-avoiding-walk analogy, and future seed-rule classification are not part of the formal end-state and are therefore recorded in excluded_aims rather than forcing framing_divergence.
